title: ZettaWorks pilot econ + ops weekly standup
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-04 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Jordan (ZettaWorks CTO), Priya (Eng Lead), Samir (Infra), Lina (Product), Carlos (Redwood CSM)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync to review pilot economics and ops metrics — tokens/sec/$, cache hit savings, batching tradeoffs, and next steps for optimization and benchmarks.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Jordan?
[00:07] Jordan (ZettaWorks): Here, sorry running a little late on my side.
[00:10] Maya (Redwood SE): No worries. We pulled together the cost dashboard and the benchmark logs, link in the notes — see "zetta-pilot-benchmarks.xlsx" (drive link).
[00:20] Priya (ZettaWorks): Got it, I'm seeing the sheet. Real quick, main objective: reduce $/MAU while keeping 95th pct latency under 300ms for the interactive flow.
[00:32] Alex: Right. Today's agenda: 1) quick readout of observed tokens/sec/$; 2) caching & prefix hit analysis; 3) batching and latency tails; 4) action items.
[00:45] Maya: On tokens/sec per dollar — we ran the hosted model (gpt-ish open variant, q4_8) and measured effective throughput normalized by spend. Baseline is ~3.1k tokens/sec/$ on the current config for mixed-length traffic. With the key-value prefix cache enabled we see effective tokens/sec/$ jump to ~4.2k — roughly a 35% improvement in unit economics. Those numbers are in sheet tab "econ-agg".
[01:15] Priya: 3.1k -> 4.2k, that's useful. How are you calculating that? Is that tokens generated per second divided by dollars per second?
[01:22] Maya: Yeah, effectively tokens/sec divided by $/sec at our current provisioned capacity. We included warm KV cache hits as avoided token generation so it's reflected. There is some noise in short runs.
[01:30] Samir: Quick question, what do you mean by "avoid token generation"? Are we skipping model compute when cache hits?
[01:36] Maya: Good callout. On prefix cache hits we serve from Redwood's cache layer and avoid autoregressive generation for the cached prefix; we still do some server-side processing for validation/filters but not full token decode. That nets the token savings.
[01:50] Lina: Does that affect latency? Like is cache return faster than cold model?
[01:54] Maya: Usually yes; cache hits returned sub-5ms in our tests versus model decode that adds tens to hundreds ms depending on batch. But note warm-up and TTL behavior matter.
[02:10] Jordan: On batching tradeoffs — the product team wants <300ms p95. Where do we stand if we push batching to 8 for cost reasons?
[02:18] Maya: We tested batch sizes 1,4,8,16. Throughput (tokens/sec) scales sublinearly; at batch=8 we saw 2.6x throughput vs batch=1. But p95 latency goes from ~220ms at batch=1 up to ~360ms at batch=8 under current load. So you trade cost for latency tail. See "batching_tradeoffs" tab.
[02:45] Priya: Hmm, 360ms p95 is above our target. Is there knob to get batching benefits but keep tail lower?
[02:52] Maya: A few levers: smaller max token limit per request, concurrency limits (to avoid large queuing), or adaptive batching where short requests bypass batching. Also you can mix dedicated instances for hot paths and hosted for cold.
[03:05] Alex: Also worth noting our dynamic routing policy can route latency-sensitive routes to a lower-batch pool while routing background flows to high-batch pools.
[03:12] Samir: On cost calc, are you including reserved capacity discounts or purely on-demand?
[03:17] Maya: The econ table currently shows on-demand hosted pricing. We added a scenario row for a Dedicated baseline at typical enterprise commit levels — that brings tokens/sec/$ up about 15% over hosted in this config.
[03:30] Jordan: What about quantization? We briefly tried q8_0 and q4_8 — any quality regression?
[03:36] Maya: q4_8 gave the best cost reduction with minimal quality drift on your eval set; first-turn rouge and API evals were within acceptable thresholds. We flagged a few prompt templates where completions were slightly truncated. We can show diffs.
[03:52] Priya: Can you surface those prompts? We need to see if they are customer-facing or internal.
[03:58] Maya: Yes, tab "eval-diffs" has the examples. We'll highlight the ones flagged as high-risk.
[04:05] Lina: Back to caching — what's the observed hit rate? Our traffic has a lot of dynamic content but many repeated system prompts.
[04:12] Maya: Observed prefix hit rate ~28% overall, but for the top 5 frequent routes it's ~62%. That distribution is why we see large aggregate savings even if global hit-rate moderate.
[04:30] Jordan: So if we expand caching rules to include a small normalized prefix for prompts we could boost hit rate?
[04:36] Maya: Exactly. Normalizing user tokens and canonicalizing system instructions increases reuse. But beware correctness: some prompts include user-specific data you can't cache.
[04:46] Alex: On operational notes — we noticed KV cache TTL of 10m led to churn; extending to 30m improved hit rate but introduced staleness risk for time-sensitive replies. Tradeoff depends on route semantics.
[05:02] Samir: Any CPU or memory pressure from larger cache TTLs?
[05:06] Maya: Minimal on the caching layer; most memory is in the cache backend. We estimated 12% increase in cache storage cost for 3x TTL on these routes. Still net positive in unit economics.
[05:20] Carlos (Redwood CSM): Quick product question — do you want us to enable adaptive batching for this pilot? It's still alpha but could help.
[05:28] Priya: Yes, let's test it in a restricted route.
[05:31] Jordan: Agree. Also can we get a percentile breakdown for compute time vs queueing time?
[05:36] Maya: Provided. In "trace-breakdown" we show compute vs queue. At p95 most of the extra time at higher batch sizes is queueing latency.
[05:50] Lina: Are there any spikes or tail events due to autoscaling?
[05:54] Maya: We saw two small spikes during the 24h window when a burst overloaded the pool and the autoscaler added capacity but with cold start latency ~2.1s for warmed model shards. We have options: pre-warm or maintain minimal spare capacity.
[06:10] Jordan: Pre-warm costs money though. How do we quantify?
[06:13] Maya: Pre-warm means a steady baseline $/hr. In our modeling a 10% spare capacity (pre-warmed) reduces observed p99 by ~60% and increases monthly cost ~7%. The ROI depends on acceptable p99.
[06:27] Priya: Let's table p99 discussion; our SLA target is p95 today.
[06:30] Alex: For next part, quick demo of the cost dashboard — Maya?
[06:33] Maya: (screen share noises) On the dashboard you can toggle cache on/off, select batch sizes, and pick quantization profiles. The "tokens/sec/$" panel updates live. Here you can see day-over-day improvements when we turned cache rules on.
[06:55] Priya: Nice. Can you export the raw traces? We need to feed into our in-house A/B analysis.
[06:59] Maya: Yes, link to raw traces in the shared drive.
[07:05] Jordan: A couple of practical asks: 1) run a 4-hour continuous benchmark at peak qps with batch=4 and batch=8; 2) stress test with synthetic liveness diffs; 3) a small POC to try adaptive batching on /chat route.
[07:20] Alex: We'll take those. I'll add as action items.
[07:25] Samir: One more — encryption/KMS: any change in cost for using customer-managed keys in Private?
[07:31] Maya: Slight increase due to HSM operations for key unwrap; negligible on token economics but can add a small fixed monthly charge for KMS integration if you go Private. We'll include that in pricing scenarios.
[07:45] Lina: Oh, competitor question — we did an internal head-to-head with Vertex and OpenAI last quarter; curious if Redwood's caching gives a unique advantage.
[07:54] Alex: Caching + dynamic routing is where we see differentiation vs vanilla endpoints; others do caching but not as integrated with routing and batching policies.
[08:05] Jordan: Any security reviews outstanding? We need SOC 2 and network diagrams for our infosec.
[08:10] Carlos: We'll share the security pack and diagram by EOD Tuesday.
[08:14] Priya: Back to numbers — can you show cost per 1M tokens in these configs?
[08:19] Maya: Sure. Baseline hosted q4_8 ~ $9.6 per 1M tokens. With caching effective spend drops to equivalent $6.8 per 1M tokens when you amortize avoided generation. Dedicated at commit reduces to approx $5.5 per 1M tokens in our model. These are ballpark in the sheet.
[08:45] Jordan: How do you reconcile per-token cost with tokens/sec/$ metric?
[08:50] Maya: tokens/sec/$ is throughput normalized by spend rate — good for ops comparisons. cost per 1M tokens is useful for billing/unit pricing. We provide both.
[09:00] Alex: Time check — we're ~9 mins in. Let's move to concrete next steps and owners.
[09:05] Maya: Action items draft: 1) 4-hr continuous benchmark at peak qps for batch 4 & 8 (Maya/Alex) due 2025-06-11; 2) Adaptive batching POC enabled on /chat restricted route (Alex/Maya) due 2025-06-18; 3) Cache normalization rule experiment on top-5 routes (Priya/Samir) due 2025-06-11; 4) Security pack share (Carlos) due 2025-06-10; 5) Update cost spreadsheet with Dedicated scenario and KMS delta (Maya) due 2025-06-09.
[09:40] Priya: Good. Also we want a short write-up on quality diffs for q4_8 for our legal/product review.
[09:45] Maya: Adding that as action: "quality diffs write-up" (Maya) due 2025-06-09.
[09:52] Jordan: One more operational note: can Redwood provide a small runbook to flip cache TTLs per route? Our oncall wants that documented.
[09:58] Carlos: We'll draft a short runbook and share in the repo.
[10:03] Alex: Anything else from Zetta?
[10:06] Lina: Not from me.
[10:07] Samir: No.
[10:08] Jordan: No, thanks. This was helpful.
[10:10] Alex: Great. We'll send the follow-up with the benchmark plan and calendar invites. Thanks everyone.
[10:15] (meeting ends)

Notes: transcript contains occasional auto-caption errors; speaker labels are best-effort. Links referenced: https://drive.redwood.ai/zetta/pilot/benchmarks and internal spreadsheet "zetta-pilot-benchmarks.xlsx"
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on pilot unit economics and operational tradeoffs. Redwood presented tokens/sec/$ baselines (3.1k -> 4.2k with caching), batching impacts (batch=8 increases throughput ~2.6x but raises p95 from ~220ms to ~360ms), KV cache behavior (28% global hit rate, 62% on top routes), quantization findings (q4_8 acceptable with minor diffs), and autoscaling/pre-warm tradeoffs. Action items agreed for benchmarking, adaptive batching POC, cache normalization tests, security docs, and cost scenarios including Dedicated/KMS deltas.
